elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Customer to assign without IBM's consent to an entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Customer.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor organization by merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor organization by acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of all or substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor organization through a sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: IBM may not assign the Agreement or any rights under it without Customer's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause states that IBM may assign 'in no event to a competitor of Customer.'

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants IBM no termination right based on Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign without consent to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no notice requirement for Customer's permitted successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: IBM has no successor-assignment exception and must obtain Customer's prior written consent for every assignment.

elements.element: Vendor must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause provides no written-notice mechanism for an IBM successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Any Customer assignment outside the enumerated affiliate and successor exceptions requires IBM's prior written consent.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that IBM's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: All IBM assignments require Customer's prior written consent, which necessarily includes assignments other than successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld, subject to the additional absolute prohibition on assignments to Customer competitors.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully implements the preferred position, including Customer's affiliate and successor carve-outs, mutualized consent restrictions, the competitor prohibition, and no IBM termination right for Customer change of control. It does not satisfy the fallback because it omits written notice for successor assignments and gives IBM no consent-free successor-assignment right. The redline is not minimal because it also changes the original continuing-liability provision from Customer-only liability to liability for either assigning party, which was not required to achieve the preferred position. The drafting otherwise preserves the operative assignment framework without contradiction.
